composing_text: 129th Infantry Brigade; 130th Infantry Brigade; 214th Infantry Brigade
notes: Landed about 24 June (Wikipedia list shows Juno); concentrated for Epsom.

current_activity: relieving Scottish infantry at Cheux; repulsing Panther attack
notes: Relieved Scottish infantry around Cheux and Sainte-Manvieu 27 June; a battalion position was counter-attacked by six 2nd Panzer Division Panthers at 09:30, attacks halted; reinforced 28 June by 32nd (Guards) Infantry Brigade; a brigade reinforced the Odon bridgehead 29 June.

current_activity: Jupiter: the reinforced division attacks Eterville, Maltot and Hill 112 at 05:00; on the slopes of the hill by 08:00
notes: Event date: 10 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 316, 317). Event definition: The 43rd Division, reinforced by the 4th Armoured, 31st Tank and 46th (Highland) Infantry Brigades, opens the attack to expand the Odon bridgehead at 05:00 on 10 July; its leading troops reach Eterville and are well up on the slopes of Hill 112 by 08:00 and the advance on Maltot follows (pp. 316-317). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 316-317: "The troops to be employed were the 43rd Division reinforced by the 4th Armoured, 31st Tank and 46th (Highland) Infantry Brigades"; "The attack was to open at 5 a.m. on the"; "leading troops of the 43rd Division reached Eterville and were well up on the slopes of Hill 112 by eight o". Location: Hill 112, Calvados (existing place PL0173) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Ellis names Hill 112, Eterville and Maltot as the objectives and the slopes of Hill 112 as reached (pp. 316-317). Context: Ellis does not name the corps on these pages; the corps is the standing relation of the division in the dataset (VIII Corps, CR0074), which the Wikipedia infobox of Jupiter (R597) also gives.

current_activity: Bluecoat: develops a 'right hook' against Cahagnes at first light and takes the village in the afternoon
notes: Event date: 31 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 392). Event definition: By first light on 31 July troops of the division, developing a 'right hook' against Cahagnes, are within striking distance when a sharp German counter-attack is driven off; Cahagnes is taken during the afternoon and late that night St. Pierre-du-Fresne is entered (p. 392); on 1 August the division continues to Point 361 (p. 392). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 392: "by first light on the morning of the 31st troops of its 43rd Division, developing a"; "Cahagnes was taken during the afternoon". Location: Cahagnes, Calvados (existing place PL0062) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Cahagnes as taken during the afternoon (p. 392).

current_activity: Mont Pincon: attacks the west face at 14:30; tanks on the top by eight o'clock; garrison eliminated by morning
notes: Event date: 6 August 1944, 14:30 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 409, 410). Event definition: After securing Ondefontaine on 5 August the division attacks the west face of Mont Pincon at 14:30 on 6 August with the 129th Brigade, the 130th Brigade assaulting the north face from Ondefontaine; seven tanks climb to the top and the rest of the squadron joins them by eight o'clock, two infantry battalions of the 129th Brigade reach the hill in the fog, and the garrison is eliminated when the fog clears in the early morning of 7 August (pp. 409-410). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 409: "The attack began at half past two on the 6th"; p. 410: "When the fog cleared in the early morning the garrison was elimin- ated and two hundred prisoners were taken". Location: Mont Pincon, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Mont Pincon (Point 361 and the hill) as the objective and the place taken (pp. 409-410).

current_activity: Crosses the Seine at Vernon in stormboats; seven of the first eight boats are lost
notes: Event date: 25 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 466). Event definition: Fifteen minutes after the corps guns open fire across the Seine from Vernon on 25 August, the first troops of the division cross in stormboats; seven of the eight boats are lost to fire from the far bank, but a battalion and a half cross during the night and fight off a number of attacks (p. 466). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 466: "the first British troops began to cross the river in stormboats"; "In spite of these mishaps a battalion and a half crossed during the night". Location: Vernon, Eure (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Vernon as the crossing place and the 43rd Division as the unit (p. 466).
